Ophthalmology · published research

Diabetic macular edema

Several small uncontrolled reports describe reduced retinal thickness or fluid, while the 135-participant sham-controlled trial found no benefit for central subfield thickness or visual acuity at four months.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Several small uncontrolled reports describe reduced retinal thickness or fluid, while the 135-participant sham-controlled trial found no benefit for central subfield thickness or visual acuity at four months.

Summary of the Evidence

Seven publications are listed in the exact diabetic-macular-edema category, all with human clinical records. Designs include a phase 2 randomized trial, open-label or single-arm series, a case report, and a translational paper that also includes animal and cell work. The two Valeda reports by Becker et al. 2021 and Kaymak et al. 2023 may contain overlapping patients; they are publications, not necessarily separate cohorts. Kaymak et al. 2023

Human and clinical evidence

The strongest direct comparison is Protocol AE, a phase 2 randomized trial at 23 US sites. It assigned 135 adults with center-involved DME and good baseline vision to a 670 nm eye patch or low-power white-light placebo. At four months, central subfield thickness increased by 13 μm with PBM and 15 μm with placebo, a mean difference of −2 μm, p=0.84. Visual acuity changes were also similar. The authors concluded that this regimen was not effective for this population. The source list also includes a four-case report, a 12-person one-year series, an individual long-term case, and small Valeda reports with stable vision and selected anatomical improvements. Kim et al. 2022

Animal evidence

The 2020 translational publication reports mouse and rat work suggesting effects on photoreceptor mitochondrial function and retinal vascular leakage. These experiments are mechanistic support only and do not overturn the null controlled human comparison.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

The same translational publication includes cultured retinal cells and reports changes in mitochondrial function and oxidative stress. The source category has no separate ex-vivo clinical evidence.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Regimens differ substantially. Protocol AE used 670 nm light for 90 seconds twice daily over four months. The Valeda series used nine multiwavelength sessions over three to four weeks. Other reports used different schedules and designs. Results in early DME with preserved acuity cannot be generalized to advanced edema or other devices.

Interpretation

The sham-controlled result carries more weight than uncontrolled before-and-after improvement. The available clinical evidence is mixed, small studies may overlap, and follow-up is limited. PBM has not shown a reliable visual or anatomical advantage for DME in the studied population and regimen.

Evidence strength in source summaryOCT anatomy: Mixed limited evidence Visual acuity: No advantage in the sham-controlled trial Symptoms: Uncertain
Publications and records7 publications: 7 human-tagged clinical records, including 1 phase 2 randomized sham-controlled trial, single-arm and open-label reports, a case report, a case series, and 1 translational human-plus-preclinical paper.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Small open-label and single-arm reports describe anatomical or subjective improvement, but a multicenter phase 2 sham-controlled trial found no difference in central retinal thickness or visual acuity after four months. Related Valeda reports may include overlapping patients. The treatment signal therefore remains inconsistent and protocol-specific.

Publication and study types

  • Study-type tags overlap for the translational paper.
  • The Valeda reports may share participants; a reliable unique cohort count is unavailable.
  • The main randomized trial enrolled 135 adults.
